name: triggers
about: Trigger points: when the playlist's voice-overs fire (seconds after the start of the track, fake clock, 50 ms ticks; each fire is a Play on Top with no playlist entry). `fires` is what the Python player measured (it includes the tick); `ideal_fires` is the time at which the playhead reaches `at` ((at - A) after the start, plus whole passes in a loop); another engine compares its own times with the IDEAL ones within `tolerance_s`.

simple._info: fires once when the playhead reaches `at` (within one 50 ms tick)

two_in_order._info: the first voice-over (3 s) is over before the second fires

trim_in_after_trigger._info: a trigger before the In point never fires

trim_out_before_trigger._info: a trigger at or after the Out point never fires (track ends at 8 s)

trigger_inside_trim._info: `at` is a position in the FILE: with A = 6 s it fires 4 s after the start

seek_over_does_not_fire._info: seeking from 1 s to 20 s jumps over the trigger at 10 s: it never fires (without the seek it would)

seek_back_rearms._info: fires at 10 s; the voice-over (3 s) is over, seek back to 2 s at 14 s of play: what is ahead is armed again, so it fires again 8 s later (22 s of play). A seek while a voice-over plays on top is ignored (the live deck is the voice-over)

loop_fires_every_pass._info: a looping 6 s window (A=0, B=6) fires in every pass (the 3 s voice-over is over before the next pass)

top_already_playing_skips._info: vo2 (8 s) is on top at 3 s, so the second trigger is skipped, not queued
